searchText: Yet another thing to consider: assuming that the current overhead calculation is working OK, that still leaves the case of using small chunks with small hashes. For example, I've made a sweep of chunk sizes = {1,2,4,8,16,32} and hash sizes = {4,8,16,32} across blocks 9M..9M+10K. The minimum overhead is 26% at chunks={4,8}(!) and hash=4 bytes. The question then would be whether 4 byte hashes would make sense, I guess. I think using we would need to think long and hard about the possible attack vectors if we used a hash size less than 32 bytes. If a hash collision could be found, then could a malicious node use that to sync different versions of the same contract? No idea, I'm not a cryptographer ;). For completeness: 16-byte hashes have a minimum overhead of 71% at chunk sizes={16,32}. 8-byte hashes have a minimum overhead of 43% at chunk sizes={8,16} I should really be looking into other things, so I will commit some changes to my tool to make this kind of sweeps easier and try to let it be
